summary: Picks one value from a short, known list in a popup. The trigger looks like an Input so forms read as one family; the list supports groups, descriptions and disabled options.
whenToUse: One choice from about 4 to 10 known options: a theme, a brand, a token group, a role.
The options are long words or labels that would crowd a RadioGroup.
Space is tight: in a toolbar, a table filter or a dense settings row (size sm).
whenNotToUse: Two or three options that should all stay visible: use RadioGroup, or an attached ButtonGroup for a view switch.
Long or unknown lists (people, repositories, 20+ tokens): use Combobox so users can type to filter.
Several values at once: use Combobox with multiple, or a CheckboxGroup.
Actions (Duplicate, Delete): use Menu. A Select changes a value, it does not run commands.

dos.title: Order options by meaning, not alphabetically by default
dos.text: Put the most common choice first, or follow the natural order (System, Light, Dark). Group long lists under short headings.

dos.title: Explain a disabled option
dos.text: A description on the option says why it cannot be picked, instead of leaving users guessing.

options.label: High contrast
options.description: Not available for the ocean brand

donts.title: A Select with two options
donts.text: Hiding two choices behind a click costs a step for nothing. Show them as radios or a Switch.

donts.title: The placeholder as an instruction
donts.text: "Click to select" says nothing. The placeholder describes the empty state: "No theme", "Any reviewer".

accessibility: Base UI Select: the trigger is a combobox button with aria-expanded; the popup is a listbox with options marked aria-selected and aria-disabled.
Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow keys open it; arrows move; typing jumps to a matching option; Enter selects; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
The Field label names the trigger; hint and error are linked through aria-describedby, and an error sets aria-invalid.
The selected option shows a check mark and a medium weight, not color alone.
The trigger edge uses color.border.strong (3:1 against surfaces) and the signal focus ring on keyboard focus.
The popup is portaled and re-applies the theme, brand and density of its trigger.
contentGuidelines: Label is a noun in sentence case: "Theme", "Brand", "Reviewer role".
Options are short, parallel nouns, sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Group headings are one or two words and never repeat the label.
Placeholders describe the empty value ("No theme"), not the action.

anatomy.trigger: Trigger box (same edge and focus as Input)
anatomy.indicator: Check mark on the selected option
